title: Local henselian ind-etale algebras are integral over the base henselization
statement: Let $f:A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with $D$ henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and ind-etale over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)$. Here $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$ means the henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$: the henselian local ring with its universal local map from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ (initial among local maps from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ to henselian local rings). The map $f$ factors through the canonical local homomorphism $A^h_{\mathfrak p}\to D$, and $D$ is integral over $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$: every element of $D$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Sentence between Theorems 6.3 and 6.4, printed p. 13: local henselian ind-etale algebras are integral over a base henselization; the prime is the contraction of the maximal ideal. Ordinary henselization: algebra.tex Tags 04GN and 04GQ.
